transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Carter (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (OrionBridge - Head of Partnerships), Ravi Singh (OrionBridge - Cloud SE), Mei Chen (OrionBridge - Dir Edge Ops)

--- Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect) ---
Quick partner intro and discovery; agreed to run benchmarks; follow-up technical deep dive and share integration docs.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood here, AE - I'll hand over to Jules for the quick tech intro but wanted to say excited to explore partnership opps with OrionBridge.
[00:12] Lena: Hi Samir, hi Jules, thanks. I'm Lena. We looked at Redwood a bit, curious about how partner integrations work and what you're expecting from infra partners.
[00:20] Jules: Thanks Lena. Quick intro, I'm Jules, SE. Redwood's runtime is focused on production inference across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. We typically work with cloud and GPU partners to validate performance and define an integration surface - e.g., private control plane, VPC peering, image artifacts, and certs.
[00:36] Ravi: Cool. quick q - what GPU types and interconnects do you generally optimize for? We run mixed clusters - A100s, some H100s, and a smaller arm of L4s for lower cost stuff.
[00:48] Jules: That's great, we support A100/H100, also M60-ish older nodes but perf is best on A100/H100. We care about interconnect - NVLink / NVSwitch when you have multi-GPU models, and network egress for hosted traffic. Our kernel selection and quantization logic picks best paths per arch. For H100, we do some specialized kernels; for L4 we suggest smaller sequence lengths or lower precision to control latency.
[01:05] Mei: we have a segmented infra - edge clusters for latency-sensitive customers and bigger centralized GPU pools. Is Redwood typically run in a dedicated capacity model or private VPC?
[01:15] Samir: Both. Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools we can colocate on partner hardware or run in your cloud region; Redwood Private is a VPC/on-prem deployment where customers want a private control plane. For partners we often do a Dedicated offering where we reserve capacity on partner infra and co-market.
[01:29] Lena: sounds promising. Commercially, we do marketplace listings and partner-managed reservations - what's typical in terms of lead routing and referral fees?
[01:37] Samir: We have a few models - co-sell, referral, or reseller. For initial pilots we usually do a revenue-share for committed capacity, then evaluate expansion. We'll send our partner program one-pager.
[01:46] Ravi: on the tech side, what do you need from us to validate performance? What benchmarks?
[01:51] Jules: Good q. Ideally: cluster specs (GPU model, counts per node), interconnect details, driver and CUDA versions, network bandwidth, and a small sample model list - e.g., a 13B decoder-only, a 34B LLM, and a smaller embedding model. We'll run throughput and p99 latency tests with typical sequence lengths. Also we look at KV cache behavior for chat workloads.
[02:10] Ravi: ok we can share that. we use Kubernetes with device plugin and some metal provisioning - not fully cloud native. Does Redwood integrate with k8s device plugins?
[02:20] Jules: Yes we have k8s support, though for partner installs we often collaborate on container images and daemons. There may be a few infra touchpoints - e.g., mount points for K/V cache persistence, NFS or local SSDs for model artifacts, and GPU driver matching.
[02:31] Samir: just to add, we'll need SSO/SAML details for pilot users, plus any compliance constraints - SOC2, ISO, so we can map controls.
[02:40] Mei: we are SOC2 in progress; we have audit logs and we use HashiCorp Vault for secrets. KMS is our customer's preference; HSM for a few customers. How does Redwood handle encryption and KMS?
[02:50] Jules: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Dedicated, we can integrate with partner KMS via standard key wrapping and we emit audit logs. We'll share our security integration doc.
[03:00] Lena: perfect. are there any common blockers you've seen with partners?
[03:04] Jules: Usually driver mismatches, weird kernel versions, or network egress for hosted APIs. Also sometimes perf drops if NVLink isn't configured or if GPU sharing policies aren't tuned - batching is sensitive. We can help with tuning suggestions.
[03:20] Ravi: latency vs cost tradeoffs - our customers often want <50ms token latency for chat but don't want to pay H100 pricing. What do you recommend?
[03:30] Samir: that's the classic tradeoff. We recommend hybrid routing: use H100 or A100x for low-latency tiers, L4 or quantized variants for best-effort or background tasks. Redwood Optimize suggests batching settings and quantization profiles by workload to balance cost/latency. We'll run a few simulated workloads on your nodes to produce concrete numbers.
[03:50] Mei: about private deployments - network and egress - customers want data residency controls. Does Redwood support region pinning?
[03:57] Jules: Yes, we support routing policies by region and can pin model versions and storage to particular regions. For private/on-prem, data never leaves the customer's VPC unless configured.
[04:06] Lena: ok, sounds like we should run a pilot. what does a pilot look like from Redwood's side?
[04:12] Samir: Typically 4-6 weeks: week 0 onboarding and infra checklist, week 1-2 benchmark runs and tuning, week 3 integration testing with your marketplace or lead routing, week 4 wrap and commercial discussion. Pricing for pilot is usually discounted and we help with co-marketing.
[04:28] Ravi: what metrics should we measure? p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per token?
[04:33] Jules: Exactly. Also memory footprint per model, model load times, and degradation modes (fallback to smaller variants). We'll produce a spreadsheet with suggested tests.
[04:43] Lena: any legal or security docs we need to review?
[04:46] Samir: We'll share SOC2 attestation, security whitepaper, and our partner terms. If you have an NDA we can loop legal in.
[04:55] Mei: we also care about monitoring and observability - how does Redwood surface per-route costs/latency?
[05:00] Jules: Redwood Console shows token-level cost breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and exportable logs. For partners we can enable per-tenant dashboards and integrate with your Prometheus/Grafana via webhooks.
[05:13] Ravi: ok great. on a practical note - how do you want to run the benchmark? do you need SSH access or a container?
[05:20] Jules: We prefer to run containerized workloads that your infra can pull. For private installs, we provide a runbook and container images. For Dedicated on partner infra, we can do a controlled cluster job. We'll need image pull creds and a list of endpoints.
[05:33] Samir: to recap next steps - Samir will send deck and partner overview; Jules will share benchmark plan; OrionBridge (Ravi) will send cluster specs and we schedule a technical deep dive next week.
[05:46] Lena: that works. small Q - have you integrated with marketplace billing systems?
[05:51] Samir: We have integrat- - integrations with major marketplaces and can support partner-managed billing in some cases. We'll validate with your marketplace team.
[06:02] Mei: any security caveats for marketplace?
[06:04] Jules: Mostly around audit logs and data flows; we'll share doc.
[06:08] Samir: ok great thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and a calendaring note for the tech deep dive.
[06:14] Ravi: thanks all. looking forward.
[06:17] Lena: thanks, bye.
